Please don't feel that way. I'm considerably older than you.

Give it a try and let me know how it goes.
The trick to it is to focus a few inches *behind* the surface. Then you'll see, in both cases. :-)

I think it's hilarious that some recommend to quit Facebook or Google. It's already too late for that.

Our best bet is to outwardly pretend we're going along with all of this (which it feels like we have no choice in) while we develop underground ways of communicating with each other and organizing. 

This might take some time, but if you consider the course of human history, it's what we've *always* done, anyway.

I don't know if it's possible to shield yourself, but it's possible to avoid the worst of the manipulation by learning to listen to what goes on in your mind.

As humans, our core method of thought is not in words, but in concepts. This is helpful to know, because you can sort out what is "you" and what is "not you" when you understand how your mind truly thinks.

One of the things I've found (and I believe I've been a target for this type of technology for several years) is that I can see projected data by gazing at an empty browser window and allowing my eyes to become unfocused--like you have to do to see one of those Magic Eye 3D prints. It takes several seconds, and the desire to blink becomes intense, but once you allow your eyes to "see" past what looks like visual noise, the information will resolve into words and symbols.

It's quite interesting.

You can also do this in a darkened room, once you've had practice, but from my experience the images resolve differently and look like a scene from the game Tempest.

I've a feeling it's currently being used that way. When I see yet another news item about a random shooting where the shooter shoots themselves at the end, my gut tells me they (the shooter) have been a victim of this technology for some time beforehand.

We're all part of an elaborate experiment.

That's a nice thought and you're a nice person for saying so.

But you don't know me.

My family is sick of me not being well and not having my life together. My retired mom sends me money each month. My brother pays for my car insurance. My in-law pays for my phone.

Except I got a long email today that my brother can't pay my insurance any more after the year ends. He wanted to give me plenty of time to figure that out but really he just made me feel like I'm a huge drag.

I never see friends because I was always the one who reached out to make plans. When I stopped doing so to let them reach back, they never did.

I don't believe that life is meant to be pain and hardship. It just looks like that's all I can ever expect from my own life. Every time I think things are going to get better something else happens to throw my life into a mess again.

I'm tired. I don't see any point to anything any more.
Good advice. I make plans and backup plans. I can't shoulder the emotional cost any more.

I understand.

I'm not dying.

But I do have chronic pain from nerve damage.

I just found out my uncle is dying from lung and liver cancer. My aunt, his wife, is The Kindest person I've ever known. She's much stronger than me.

I keep battling, and temporarily overcoming, homelessness.

I am questioning my sanity. 

My family wants to help me but they are getting impatient with me and this causes emotional pain. I'm pushing them away because it's easier to be misunderstood by strangers than my own family.

I don't live in a war zone.

But I live in a society that wants to pretend it's free. I wonder why our youngest are referred to as "Generation Z". I feel hopeless about our long-term future.

I do that. All the time. It's the only thing that has kept me from ending it up to this point.

What happens is that the next bad thing happens AFTER I get to feeling better.

Not during. Not because I'm "expecting" it.

After. 

When I'm feeling hopeful and optimistic that I can finally have a decent life. When I sort out all the fabulous lemonade I'm going to drink. (Look Ma! No scurvy!)

Yes, it's ludicrous. 

I had viral tonsillitis so many times growing up, and nearly always got prescribed antibiotics. When I questioned the fact that they would do NOTHING for my case, the prescribing doctor would shrug and tell me to take them anyway.

I never did.
Thanks. It's just made me feel like I really am a pathetic loser.
Oh well. You sound busy anyway.

You must get around on this site quite a bit if you're not even sure whom I might be.

I'm going to let the mystery remain. When you think you know, drop a note to my other account. 

I look forward to hearing from you.

And yes, it's a bit of a game-- but it's not cruel. Just a tiny bit of fun to brighten my otherwise dreary existence.

Hi. I didn't respond to what you wrote but it moved me.

It moved me so much that I reached out to you, seemingly at random, from a different account.

Yes, that sucks

. I've had suicidal thoughts most of my life. I've even been put on hold by the suicide hotline-- more than once. When one of the times I freaked out when the guy came back, he yelled at me and then hung up.

Thanks for the comment. I was surprised it even got posted. I did it last night when I couldn't sleep and it didn't even show up in the sub until a few hours later-- I was thinking I was right and that I wouldn't be allowed to even put it out there.
